title: Zero Array Transformation III
summary: Given an integer array nums and a series of queries, each query specifies a range to decrement elements by at most 1.
statement: Given an integer array nums and a series of queries, each query specifies a range to decrement elements by at most 1. Determine the maximum number of queries that can be removed while still allowing nums to be converted to a zero array. If conversion is impossible, return -1.
constraints: nums and queries each contain up to 100,000 entries.
A retained range may independently decrement every covered index by zero or one.
Remove as many whole queries as possible while retaining enough coverage at every index, or return -1.
hints: When index i lacks coverage, some currently available query must be kept.
Choose the range ending farthest right so the forced selection helps the most future indices.
Sort by start, push eligible ends into a max-heap, and record each selected range’s expiration in a difference array.
The exchange choice never hurts current coverage and dominates any shorter available range for every later position.
editorial: The exchange choice never hurts current coverage and dominates any shorter available range for every later position.

tests.explanation: The two full ranges satisfy indices zero and two, so the middle-only query is removable.
Keeping ranges [0,2] and [1,3] covers all indices, allowing two removals.
